task_name: Add finance role, request-time authorization, and payment terms

concerns_addressed: Cycle 1 migration finding resolved: the PostgreSQL branch explicitly discovers and drops role-related CHECK constraints, adds a replacement constraint including finance, leaves the existing role default untouched, and the down path converts finance rows to outlet before restoring the original allowed-role set (apps/api/database/migrations/2026_09_10_000023_add_finance_role_to_users.php:18-68).

Cycle 1 authentication finding resolved: Authenticate.php no longer globally denies finance; deny.finance is applied only to unrelated administration routes, while finance-capable payment routes remain outside that middleware. FinanceAuthorizationService performs current-database role and active-user checks, and the existing JWT response/custom-claim shape is unchanged.

Prior environment concern: SQLite migration verification passed. PostgreSQL migration could not be executed because the local PHP environment lacks the PostgreSQL driver. Static verification was used for PostgreSQL and found no remaining design defect.

strengths: FinanceAuthorizationService centralizes request-time database role checks and requires active users (apps/api/app/Services/FinanceAuthorizationService.php:14-40).

Role assignment/removal uses a transaction and row lock, audits only actual role changes, guards inactive targets, and makes repeated assignment idempotent (apps/api/app/Services/FinanceRoleService.php:11-57).

Unrelated administration denial is route-scoped through a middleware alias rather than a global authentication behavior; payment/finance-capable routes are not globally blocked (apps/api/routes/api.php:35-108).

Payment-term validation is integer and bounded to 1–90, and the model provides the seven-day null fallback (apps/api/app/Http/Requests/SetPaymentTermRequest.php:18-22; apps/api/app/Models/Outlet.php:49-52).

The PostgreSQL migration uses escaped catalog-derived constraint names and explicit SQL, with a reversible down path; no broad permission graph, multi-role model, mocked auth/database, or auth response redesign was introduced.
